# K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills — source dossier

**State:** M6 source inventory and local coverage comparison complete; one narrow technique is implemented and release verification remains open. No upstream setup script, agent workflow, or dependency install has been run. The independent OpenCitations public API was probed through the new local MCP tool without credentials.

## Pinned source and reuse boundary

- Upstream: [K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills), pinned at [`49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/commit/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18). The clean, filtered local checkout is ignored at `references/work/k-dense-scientific-agent-skills/` and is temporary.
- The root [LICENSE.md](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/LICENSE.md) declares MIT and copyright 2025 K-Dense Inc. Individual script, data, model, and service terms require separate assessment before adoption; the root license alone does not settle them.
- The pinned tree has 2,484 tracked files and 166 `skills/*/SKILL.md` files. [`plugin.json`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/plugin.json) declares version 2.69.0 and the Agent Plugins schema. A full source and local-coverage inventory follows below.

## Evidence limits

K-Dense's [resource paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.00065v2) describes a 163-skill earlier snapshot and explicitly reports no task-level evaluation or host selection rate. At that older tag, resident descriptions used 14,246 tokens (7.1% of a 200,000-token window), and loading every reference file would overflow the window in 29 of 46 documented workflows. Its CI ran only 20 of 105 script-bearing skill suites, and none of its gates established scientific validity. These figures are context for assessing this pinned 166-skill tree, not measurements of our host. Selected techniques must pass this campaign's real harness and scientific-boundary checks; the whole catalog will not be installed.

## Source architecture and operational assumptions

The tree stores one skill per `skills/<slug>/` directory, with a `SKILL.md` instruction file and optional `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/`. [`docs/skills.md`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/docs/skills.md) lists all 166 exactly once under documentation categories; it is not a runtime selector. The frontmatter's name and description are the routing surface, while compatibility and allowed-tools describe host assumptions. The [`plugin.json`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/plugin.json) manifest packages the whole tree for plugin-capable hosts. It supplies no confined execution runtime or Co-Scientist integration by itself.

| Documentation family | Skills |
|---|---:|
| Scientific Databases & Data Access | 10 |
| Scientific Integrations | 11 |
| Scientific Packages | 128 |
| Scientific Thinking & Analysis | 17 |

All 166 declare name, description, and metadata version; 162 declare a license, 119 compatibility, and 102 allowed-tools. The pinned tree has 106 script-bearing skill directories with 535 Python, 2 shell, and 122 XML/XSD support files. There are 130 test modules across 107 skill suites. [`tests/skill-requirements.toml`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/tests/skill-requirements.toml) lists 162 skill dependency entries, including 18 marked unavailable; version and interpreter requirements can conflict. The upstream [`tests/run_all.py`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/tests/run_all.py) isolates suites with `uv` and may download packages or interpreters. Neither it nor upstream agent workflows were run here. Source inspection and the paper distinguish tests of structural or script behavior from scientific validity.

The repo's [`scan_skills.py`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/scan_skills.py) can send skill text to a credentialed LLM and defaults to a model without a verified free billing path. Other skills can call OpenRouter, Parallel, lab, clinical, or cloud services; their `allowed-tools` strings are advisory, not a sandbox. Campaign experiments must omit ambient credentials, keep metered services unavailable, and use the current workspace's confinement and provenance controls. A local validator is only a structural check, not evidence that a hypothesis is scientifically correct.

## Component terms and attribution

Four bundled document-format skills, `docx`, `pdf`, `pptx`, and `xlsx`, declare proprietary terms in their own `LICENSE.txt` files, so the root MIT license does not authorize copying them. The `deepspot-m` skill declares PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, `what-if-oracle` declares CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, three skills have unknown terms, and four omit a license field. The [`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/CITATION.cff) requests a paper citation and the exact release or commit. Any selected component needs its own terms, author metadata, script dependencies, and data/model licenses checked before reuse. No upstream code has been copied.

## Comparison targets, not adoption decisions

The [`hypothesis-generation`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/skills/hypothesis-generation/SKILL.md) skill includes evidence-led rival predictions and local validators; [`scientific-brainstorming`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/skills/scientific-brainstorming/SKILL.md) has decision registers; [`peer-review`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/skills/peer-review/SKILL.md) has claim/evidence audit scaffolds; and [`experimental-design`](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/blob/49c6e97775eaa18ba791bebe23162a70ae601c18/skills/experimental-design/SKILL.md) documents controls and randomization. Database and paper-lookup skills include reproducible retrieval rules. Their local counterparts, overlaps, and actual workflow value must be assessed before any integration. The root README's database-family count and license-field generalization differ from the pinned catalog and frontmatter census; the tracked files govern this assessment.

## Local harness baseline for comparison

Co-Scientist currently vendors the separate [Google DeepMind Science Skills](../../vendor/science-skills/) bundle at the revision in the root [NOTICE](../../NOTICE). The API image exposes 32 of its 38 skills; four have no runnable script and two require omitted heavy dependencies. `engine/src/co_scientist/skills/catalog.py` reads a single `COSCIENTIST_SKILLS_DIR`, advertises capped one-line summaries, withholds skills it knows cannot run, and lets `read_skill` fetch a document or path-contained reference on demand. The model runs scripts via the ordinary confined workspace command tool, not a separate runtime. The drafting pass is the only production consumer, on extended/ultra tiers, and reads at most two skills. `campaign_free_mode()` currently disables that surface entirely; changing this requires its own zero-cost and confinement proof.

The default MCP configuration already exposes literature retrieval (PubMed/PMC, OpenAlex, Europe PMC, preprints, arXiv and guarded web), ChEMBL, UniProt, ClinicalTrials.gov, STRING, Reactome, Open Targets, Ensembl and gnomAD. The DeepMind bundle adds selected resources and workflow scripts, so overlapping database names alone do not identify a gap. The existing skill path has scoped command provenance, report attribution, a credential allowlist disabled for campaign mode, and workspace containment. Its `.licenses/` seeding recognizes the DeepMind bundle's notice pattern; it does not prove compliance with a different component's terms.

Offering the full K-Dense catalog through the current 160-character summary rule would add about 21,161 prompt characters per drafting turn, versus about 5,156 for the current 38-entry bundle before the six withheld entries. This is a local character-count estimate, not a model-token or quality evaluation. All pinned K-Dense `SKILL.md` files are under the current 60,000-character document cap, but selected reference files and transcript growth still matter. The comparison should select by an observed workflow gap and then test the selected item's actual routing, execution, dependencies and attribution.

## Coverage comparison and candidate register

All K-Dense mechanisms below are **external techniques**, not evidence of Google's private implementation. Retaining the present graph, retrieval tools, report gates, and separate DeepMind bundle is a **local design choice**. The paper-backed Google behaviors already represented by generation, adversarial review, Elo ranking, and literature grounding are assessed through the project's existing parity records, not inferred from this source. Candidate IDs remain stable across later decisions. "Open" means the behavior has not passed an adoption or rejection test; it is not a negative result.

The separate DeepMind bundle already contains an AlphaFold structure fetch/analysis skill and a UniBind dataset skill. Their operations are not present as default MCP tools, but that is a local exposure question, not a K-Dense code adoption: K-Dense provides database references, while the actual scripts and licenses belong to the pinned DeepMind vendor. Any future exposure needs its own real response, source terms, bounded download, and provenance assessment. Eight INDRA CoGEx tools are registered locally but intentionally absent from default selection. This distinction prevents counting a named database as an executable Co-Scientist capability.

### KDS-HYP-01 fit check

The existing [INDRA golden-run receipt](../../evaluations/results/golden-run-indra-2026-07-12.json) records a completed real engine run, 18 report hypotheses, six PubMed evidence records and 12 located support spans on a public research goal; [parity verification](../../docs/PARITY-VERIFICATION.md) documents the real-source boundary. The retained receipt includes a goal, counts and evidence samples, but not the individual hypothesis bodies or K-Dense's linked preregistration fields. The local `Hypothesis` model stores an experiment as text, not typed rivals, predictions, measurements, estimands and analyses. The M1 and M2 campaign-owned live runs have no completed hypothesis to substitute. This is a source-data fit limitation, not a failed scientific-quality score.

After inspecting the source validator's imports, file I/O, parser and entry point, it was run once on that retained receipt with `env -i` and no ambient credentials. It exited 2 and named 19 missing mandatory top-level fields, including `hypotheses`, `predictions`, `causal_estimands`, `operationalizations`, and `analysis_plan`. No output file, network call, model call or upstream setup occurred. The original proposal to validate one individual completed local hypothesis cannot be satisfied from the retained public-input artifacts: only a run receipt survives, and fabricating the missing 19 fields would invalidate the test. Options were to add a new persisted research-plan model, rerun a paid or rate-limited provider for a fresh artifact, or reject the whole-record validator; the last fits the existing product and zero-spend boundary. No K-Dense code was copied.

### KDS-CITE-02 current service policy check

On 2026-09-23, the official [OpenCitations Index v2 API documentation](https://api.opencitations.net/index/v2) states a 180 requests/minute per-IP limit; the pinned K-Dense guide's "no published per-second cap" must not be treated as no rate limit. The official [access-token page](https://opencitations.net/accesstoken/) says a token is voluntary and free, and the [OpenCitations site](https://opencitations.net/) says the data are CC0 and access is without charge. The API documentation confirms prefixed `doi:`/`pmid:`/`omid:` identifiers, index-prefixed merged records, and separate count and edge endpoints.

A no-credential, read-only probe against the official v2 endpoint used `doi:10.1108/jd-12-2013-0166` and returned incoming count `57`, outgoing count `45`, and 45 outgoing reference rows. One row contained an OCI and separately prefixed citing/cited identifiers, including DOIs. The two count calls preceded the bounded 45-row edge fetch; no API token, model, plugin or metered service was used. The probe proves endpoint availability and response shape only. A citation edge is neither a paper abstract nor evidence that one work supports another, and the current engine's text search cannot consume these edge rows as ordinary paper hits.

**Selected route and acceptance boundary:** independently implement a narrow read-only MCP operation in the existing literature server, not the K-Dense `paper-lookup` bundle or a second network runtime. Offer it to the existing tool-calling draft path with instructions to use it only for a known DOI and relevant graph question; never automatically expand every literature query. A count-first hard cap prevents an unpaginated high-degree fetch. The tool interface must return direction, identifiers, OCI, source URL and access time; validate identifiers; distinguish zero indexed edges from upstream failure; and preserve the existing campaign public-tool and confined workflow boundaries. The acceptance check is an actual call through `/mcp`, not schema registration alone, plus deterministic transport tests for cap, malformed response and errors. There is no scientific-quality improvement claim from adding a citation-list operation, so a new LLM ranking benchmark is not its acceptance test. Retrieval quality would need a separately declared paired evaluation before making that claim. The source contributes endpoint-selection and failure-mode guidance under MIT; no K-Dense source code is copied.

The affected public-interface test failed red when `/mcp` did not advertise `get_opencitations_citation_edges`, then passed after registering the tool. Eleven targeted MCP tests pass, and the draft provider contract confirms the schema reaches only that configured tool-calling path. A credential-empty live invocation through an in-process FastMCP `/mcp` transport fetched the official service on 2026-09-23: `citation_count=57`, `reference_count=45`, incoming status `count_exceeds_edge_limit`, outgoing status `complete`, 45 outgoing edges, and first OCI `06180334099-0616067039`. The invocation sent three OpenCitations requests and no model request. The tool returns URL/time/OCI and a statement that citation links do not establish claim support. Red/green regressions cover index-prefixed merged identifiers without splitting semicolons inside DOI suffixes, and a count of 50 followed by 51 edge rows; the latter now fails rather than truncating and falsely reporting `complete`. The raw identifier fields are retained for provenance. A process-wide monotonic pacer spaces requests one second apart across concurrent event loops, below the published per-IP limit for this one process, with no 429 retry. Local release-suite and deployed-service checks are recorded separately below when complete.

The first `make test-all` run exposed four failing campaign-admission tests: the server's public-tool list included the new operation while the separately packaged engine client's expected list did not. Adding the same name to `co_scientist.mcp_campaign.PUBLIC_TOOLS` restored agreement. The new client accepts exactly the old or new reviewed public manifest during the API-first, MCP-second rollout; a red/green admission regression rejects any additional unqualified tool. This is an integration defect caught before release, not a hosted-CI result.

### Local acceptance and staged release

The final local release checks passed 3,146 engine tests (two pre-existing skips), 1,892 app tests, 294 MCP tests plus strict MCP mypy, 115 parity rows and the evaluation test suite, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make build`, `make eval-smoke`, and 753 frontend unit tests across 125 files. The MCP suite initially exposed a Brave-only test that inherited a configured Tavily fallback when the new server test imported the MCP server; the test now clears that fallback, and the full MCP suite passes. The parity gate initially caught an 86-line new function against its 40-line ceiling; the fetch, normalization and directional assembly are now separate helpers, and the full parity/evaluation suite passes. These fixes changed no production web-search behavior. The initial `make e2e` run passed 12 cases and timed out three completed-run cases at the harness's 60-second limit while other checks were competing for the local machine; all three failed cases then passed in isolated browser runs, including loading a completed report and its decision history. The initial aggregate browser run remains a failure and is not represented as green. This tool has no new UI flow.
